static_traits.name: Chen Ming
static_traits.family_status: The youngest of 8 siblings; having a close circle of friends
static_traits.social_status: Supportive friendships, but not yet sharing work troubles with them; work performance affected
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before; not yet received psychotherapy or counseling; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to reflect; low mood; fairly cooperative in counseling; tending toward self-reproach and using extreme statements

basic_info.main_problem: Because the first meeting did not close a real estate deal, I feel I am a very incompetent and useless salesperson.
basic_info.core_demands: The persistent self-criticism and sense of incompetence are affecting my self-esteem and work performance, so I am seeking counseling.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / unqualified

special_situations.event: The first meeting with a client not yet closing a real estate deal
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot close the deal at the first meeting, it means I am not good enough and not suited for sales
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replays meetings; works hard to improve sales skills and client interaction to prove himself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I completely failed; I am not suited for sales

special_situations.event: Before and after facing new potential clients
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure means all future failures
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive tension and self-reproach before meetings, trying to avoid failure through fuller preparation

special_situations.event: Obvious physical discomfort (stomach in knots) when recalling that failed meeting each time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The fact that I feel terrible right now means things really are terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labeling the failure as a global self-label, reinforcing negative emotions to drive self-improvement

special_situations.event: When asked about past successful interactions, still feels this failure matters more
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past successes cannot prove my competence; this failure is the key evidence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Fixates on negative details, ignores or belittles positive evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those successes are not important; this failure is what matters

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as capable and to achieve career success
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure being negated, being labeled 'incompetent'
defense_goal: Preventing failure through self-reproach and high standards, maintaining control of the situation to lower anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a failure-prone practitioner

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites him to look for positive evidence or recall successful experiences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these successes 'do not count', only failure defines self-worth
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Firm but not excessive tone, repeatedly emphasizing the importance of failure while downplaying or ignoring the meaning of successes.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing the failed meeting and trying to find the problem
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing failure as negation of overall self-ability, thus avoiding directly experiencing shame and helplessness
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses an analytical tone, lists meeting details and reasoning processes in detail, minimizing the expression of emotion vocabulary and subjective feelings.

manifestations: Not yet confiding work setbacks and self-criticism to friends, choosing to bear the pressure alone
Binding self-worth to one outcome in high-pressure situations, finding it hard to build empathic support with others
outcomes: Decreased social confidence, weakened connection with support systems

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Intense self-criticism and doubting their abilities
Not expressing difficulties in front of friends, cautiously holding back troubles

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats 'the first meeting should close the deal' as a hard standard
Evaluates self-worth by outcome-oriented, absolutist standards

exception_events.target_problem: In facing potential clients, the client usually thinks catastrophically with self-denial, rising anxiety, leading to declining performance.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In several client meetings before, the client felt more confident, the process smoother, less stress, and did not take one outcome as negation of overall ability.
exception_events.reason: Clues: lower anxiety, less focus on failure, being in a more relaxed state, thus able to be more engaged and maintain confidence at the time.

positive_force: Having a supportive circle of friends (though not yet activated)
Has had successful client interactions and confident experiences that can serve as evidence
Actively trying to improve sales skills and client interactions
negative_force: Marked cognitive biases (catastrophizing, black-and-white, overgeneralization, predicting the future, mental filtering, personalization)
Rigid performance standards (the first meeting must close the deal)
High anxiety levels in work situations, strong sense of pressure
Not asking friends for help leaving support not yet activated, increased sense of isolation

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing and self-denial in work situations, with anxiety and physical tension (stomach in knots)
antecedent: After the first meeting did not close the deal
Before and after facing potential clients
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjecting 'closing on the first try' as an absolute standard, and overgeneralizing one failure into inadequate ability and worthlessness.
target_behavior.function: Gaining surface control through anticipating the worst and self-criticism, lowering expectations to avoid renewed disappointment and uncertainty.
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, decline in work performance, lowered social confidence, negative emotions spreading in work and life.

target_behavior.behavior: Not expressing work troubles and emotions to friends
antecedent: Rising stress when recalling failure experiences
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being evaluated and negated (personalization tendency), to preserve self-image and avoid shame.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible external evaluation and discomfort, briefly reducing vulnerability under others' gaze.
target_behavior.consequence: Support system not yet used, insufficient emotion-regulation resources, sense of isolation and anxiety maintained and worsened
